intro.title: Mireille's shop
paragraphs: Your grandmother Mireille was the town's perfumer for fifty years.
She left you her shop on the square: the organ, her shelves, three bottles still half full, and her formula book.
The book is a mess of coffee rings and smudged ink, and most of the amounts have run into nothing. But the town remembers what she made.

letter.heading: Tucked inside the cover of her book
body: If you're reading this, the shop is yours. Don't be frightened of the organ. Smell everything twice, write everything down, and let people talk: they'll tell you what they want if you listen.
The pages that matter most are the ones people still wear. Ask them.

people.name: Agathe
people.about: She was married in the town church, and Mireille made her wedding cologne.

people.name: Josette
people.about: The baker from across the square, flour still on her sleeves.

people.name: Henri
people.about: The clockmaker. His late wife wore one of Mireille's ambers every winter.

people.name: Lucien
people.about: The retired postman, who knew every house in town and every one of Mireille's perfumes.

requests.greeting: So you're Mireille's grandchild. You have her hands.
requests.retryGreeting: Shall we try my wedding cologne again? I've been thinking about it all week.
requests.thanks: That's it. That's exactly it. She'd be so proud of you.

brief.memory: Your grandmother made the cologne I wore at my wedding. Bright as lemons when I walked up the aisle, and lavender all through the dancing. My granddaughter is getting married. Could you make it again?
hints: It wasn't sweet at all. Clean, like washing on the line.
Right at the very end there was something warm, just a whisper of it.

requests.greeting: Bonjour! I've owed your grandmother something for years.
requests.giveText: Mireille lent me this for my custards and I never gave it back. Vanillin: it's what makes vanilla smell like vanilla. Everything on your shelves is so serious. I'd like something sweeter.
requests.thanks: Oh, that's the bakery. That's my whole life in a bottle.

brief.memory: The bakery at five in the morning, before anyone else in town is awake.
hints: Sweeter than anything you've made so far, I'd guess.
A little lemon zest in the dough, and a dark crust.

requests.greeting: Josette says you have Mireille's vanilla back. Then perhaps you can help me.
requests.retryGreeting: I'd like to try the amber again, if you'll humour an old man.

brief.memory: Every winter Mireille made my wife an amber. Warm as the stove in my workshop, and sweet as the cake she always burned a little.
hints: A bright moment at the very start, like opening the door to the cold.
Mostly that dark, warm resin, with the sweetness underneath.

requests.greeting: Henri's been showing everyone his wrist. My turn.
requests.retryGreeting: Back for my Sunday best. Third time lucky?
requests.thanks: My Sunday best. I'll wear it to lunch.

brief.memory: My Sunday best. Mireille made it the year I retired: lavender, but softer, and it lasted right through lunch.
hints: Mostly lavender, but not like soap. Rounder.
Sweet and warm underneath, like the bottom of a biscuit tin.

pages.title: Cologne for Agathe's wedding
pages.margin: Bright for the vows, soft for the dancing. Only a drop of the resin, or it turns heavy.

lesson.text: An eau de cologne is a light splash led by citrus oils such as bergamot, with herbs like lavender, worn generously and gone within a couple of hours. The style takes its name from the city of Cologne, where it was sold from the early 1700s.

pages.title: Winter amber, for Henri's wife
pages.margin: Half the bottle is resin. The sweet one stays longest; keep it under the labdanum.

lesson.text: An amber accord pairs a dark, leathery resin like labdanum with vanilla sweetness. Vanillin, the molecule that gives vanilla most of its smell, was first made in a laboratory in 1874, and warm ambers built on it became popular in the early 1900s.
check: lesson: the early-1900s date for ambers built on vanillin

pages.title: Lucien's Sunday best
pages.margin: Lavender first and most. A little of the sweet and the resin to round it, one drop of bergamot to wake it up.

lesson.text: Lavender is a heart note: it opens herbal and fresh and fades within a few hours. A sweet, resinous base under it makes it rounder and helps it last.

pages.title: For the shop
pages.margin: Nearly blank. Just a title, in her best handwriting, and nothing underneath.
